messages:
Liam O'Connor: Hi all — first day here, trying to boot the local stack but Postgres fails in compose.
Liam O'Connor: Error: "FATAL: could not bind IPv4 socket: Address already in use" from postgres container logs.
Liam O'Connor: My docker-composepostgres portion is just:
```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
    ports:
      - 5432:5432
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```
Liam O'Connor: I'm on Ubuntu 22.04 (work laptop) and I *think* I already have Postgres installed via apt. Not sure if that matters.
Riya Shah: welcome! yep that matters — host Postgres will already be listening on 5432 so binding host port 5432 in compose fails.
Riya Shah: quick check: run `sudo ss -ltnp | grep 5432` or `lsof -iTCP:5432 -sTCP:LISTEN -P -n` to see what process owns the port.
Liam O'Connor: running that shows `postgres  1234  0.0  ...` — so it's the system postgres.
Elliot Gomez: two options: 1) stop the host postgres while you use compose (`sudo systemctl stop postgresql`) or 2) remap the container port to a different host port, e.g. `- 55432:5432`.
Elliot Gomez: If your app connects to localhost:5432 you can change its env var to point at 55432 when developing.
Liam O'Connor: ah ok. Is there a recommended approach for new hires? I don't want to break my system postgres.
Samir Patel: recommended: avoid changing your system services. Use remapped port (55432) or use Docker named networks and have your services talk to the db by service name (db) without exposing to host at all.
Samir Patel: If you don't need host access (psql from host), edit compose to remove `ports:` and let the app connect to `db:5432` on the user-defined network.
Liam O'Connor: we do have some local scripts that run psql from host though. Any tips for that?
Riya Shah: you can run `docker-compose exec db psql -U postgres` or `docker run --rm --network <project> postgres:14 psql -h db -U postgres` so you don't need host port exposed.
Elliot Gomez: also watch out for the bind-mount `./pgdata` permissions — if you used a host folder with root owned files you'll see permission errors. Prefer a named volume: `volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` and `volumes: { pgdata: {} }` at the bottom.
Liam O'Connor: cool. I switched to `- 55432:5432` for now and updated my .env to point to 55432 and `docker-compose up` worked. Migrations ran.
Opsbot: FYI: onboarding doc updated at https://intranet.redwood.com/dev/local-postgres-note (new-hires guidance: prefer 55432 or named volumes).
Liam O'Connor: Thanks everyone — leaving the system postgres alone and using 55432 for the dev stack. Appreciate the quick help!
